title: Entitlements and Usage
governing_sources: specification/volume-ii/contracts/S-02.json (MTX-053: PRULE-002 bootstrap BillingEntity/Plan Assignment invariant, consumed not redefined)
specification/volume-ii/contracts/S-07.json (MTX-058: the crawl.start Decision/reservation at Queued -> Running, consumed not redefined)
od_006_position: OD-006 `Current Status` is Ratified 2026-07-17, ratified as specified, `Blocking Impact: None`. The approved option is Option 3 as implemented: high-cost operations hard-block only when `committed_units + active_reserved_units + requested_units` would EXCEED the active hard limit, equality is allowed, after an atomic server-side check and reservation; low-cost report, history, Issue, recommendation and score reads remain warning-only AT the usage hard limit while the Organization and the human Account or tenant service identity remain active. WF-015's own prose still calls this 'the OD-006 interim policy' and says the classification 'does not approve the final grace policy'. That prose predates the ratification session and is not a status source. The soft/hard behaviour contracted here is settled authority and is implemented, not withheld. OD-005 makes the numerals versioned policy configuration bound to an approved policy version rather than Volume I constants; the current approved values are `entitlement-interim-v1`'s, and a numeric change is a policy-version change.
od_019_position: OD-019 `Current Status` is Ratified 2026-07-17, ratified as specified, `Blocking Impact: None`. `read-metering-v1` is approved and defines exactly the three things Volume II previously recorded as missing: the response unit (one record per accepted top-level document read), the exhaustive route-to-operation declaration (every metered read route statically declares exactly one of the five low-cost operations; an undeclared route resolves `operation_unknown` and Blocks with `contact_support`, so it is unreachable rather than silently unmetered), and the durable replay identity (Read Decision IDs are server-minted deterministically from Organization, human Account or service identity, declared operation, resolved target identity and state version, and counter window). The metering semantics are therefore contracted in full here and are NOT a withheld limb.
low_cost_metering_authority: Recorded contradiction, not an invention. `APPLICATION_LAYER.md#UPSTREAM-V1-LOW-COST-METERING-005` states that composite page/frame charging and the physical metered-read replay identity 'remain disabled until controlled Volume I clarification', and the Query Contract repeats that `Workflows::Wf015::LowCostRead` 'is not executable until UPSTREAM-V1-LOW-COST-METERING-005 resolves its durable-response identity'. OD-019's Ratified Behavior supplies every one of those answers. API_CONTRACTS.md's Query Transport already reads the register correctly -- 'deferred under `UPSTREAM-V1-LOW-COST-METERING-005`, which OD-019 resolves by ratifying the metered-read unit; their transport exposure is intentionally deferred to the Volume II baseline'. That is the correct division and the one S-22 adopts: the metering SEMANTICS are ratified and are contracted here in full; only the physical GET path exposure is deferred to the Volume II transport baseline owned by API_CONTRACTS.md, which is the ordinary route answer and not an owner-decision block. Treating the stale blocker prose as a live gate would withhold behaviour the owner approved, which is the failure mode RATIFICATION_STATUS_OVERLAY.md exists to prevent. Correcting the two APPLICATION_LAYER.md paragraphs is a separate governed edit and is not performed by this contract.
operation_string_is_not_a_permission: The five low-cost operation strings are metering classes, not authorization tokens, and the coincidence is load-bearing. `issue.read` and `recommendation.read` exist in both the Permission Baseline and the operation map; `report.view`, `history.view` and `score.read` do NOT exist as permissions at all -- the Permission Baseline's reads are `issue.read`, `score.summary.read`, `score.detail.read`, `history.read`, `recommendation.read`, `evidence.metadata.read`, `evidence.payload.read`, `evidence.restricted.read`, `entitlement.notice.read`, `security.notice.read`, `export.retrieve`, plus the OD-020 rows. A read is authorized by its own named permission and metered by its declared operation; neither substitutes for the other, and no permission may be inferred from an operation name.
reservation_consumption: S-07's MTX-058 already contracts the `crawl.start` Decision and reservation obtained atomically at the `Crawl.Queued -> Crawl.Running` commit and committed or released exactly once at the Crawl durable point. S-22 supplies the WF-015 machinery that decision consumes -- the counter window, the Decision record, the reservation lifecycle, the lease and the commit/release rule -- and does not redefine when a Crawl reserves. The same relationship holds for `reassessment.start`, `ai.generate` and `export.generate`, whose protected execution checkpoints belong to their own workflows.

MTX-040.interface_type: Two unrelated surfaces under one workflow. (1) Enforcement: server-side decision checkpoints with no actor-facing interface -- a low-cost read about to reach its durable response checkpoint, or an immediate or queued high-cost operation about to execute its first protected side effect. (2) Policy management: a synchronous authenticated command activating an immutable Entitlement Policy version. The two share no permission and no actor; WF-015's Authorization is explicit that only the server-side entitlement service identity makes decisions.
MTX-040.route: Split by limb. Policy management HAS a route: API_CONTRACTS.md registers `POST /api/v1/organizations/:organization_id/entitlement-policies` -> `ActivateEntitlementPolicy`, permission `policy.entitlement.manage`, policy-conditional `If-Match`, `201`, attributes `ATTR-ActivateEntitlementPolicy` (`candidate: object<EntitlementPolicyCandidate>`, `plan_approval_id: uuid`). Enforcement has none and must not acquire one - `DecideEntitlement`, `ReserveEntitlement`, `HeartbeatEntitlement`, `CommitEntitlement`, `ReleaseEntitlement` and `RecordLowCostUsage` are internal checkpoints of the operation being gated, and an inbound endpoint that let a client assert a Decision would be exactly the client-side trust WF-015's Security Notes prohibit. The five low-cost read GET paths remain listed in API_CONTRACTS.md as blocked mappings returning transport `404`: their metering semantics are ratified under OD-019 and contracted here, while their transport exposure is owned by API_CONTRACTS.md at the Volume II baseline.
MTX-040.request_schema: Enforcement request envelope: Organization, exactly one human Account ID or tenant-scoped service identity ID (both forms or neither is a schema rejection), operation string, requested units, idempotency key. Policy command: complete immutable `EntitlementPolicyCandidate` (`policy_schema_version=entitlement-policy-v1`, `semantic_version`, `activation_mode=immediate`, `rules`), expected current policy version, `plan_approval_id`, and no client-supplied effective or expiry time. `EntitlementPolicyRules.operation_rules` has exactly the nine keys `crawl.start`, `reassessment.start`, `ai.generate`, `export.generate`, `report.view`, `history.view`, `issue.read`, `recommendation.read`, `score.read`; a missing or duplicate class makes the policy invalid.
MTX-040.response_schema: The immutable Entitlement Decision with every field in the WF-015 Decision contract; for a high-cost Allow or AllowWithWarning, its one Reservation and current state; for an allowed low-cost read, the authorized response plus its one LowCostUsageRecord. Policy activation returns the new active policy version with commit-time effectiveness assigned and the prior version superseded.
MTX-040.controller: Only for the policy limb: the registered JSON command controller and its browser twin for `POST /api/v1/organizations/:organization_id/entitlement-policies`, which constructs the logical command and invokes exactly one `Workflows::Wf015::Handlers::ActivateEntitlementPolicy`. Enforcement has no controller - a controller MUST NOT call an entitlement checkpoint directly; the low-cost path reaches it only through the `Workflows::Wf015::LowCostRead` coordinator.
MTX-040.command: `Workflows::Wf015::DecideEntitlement`, `ReserveEntitlement`, `HeartbeatEntitlement`, `CommitEntitlement`, `ReleaseEntitlement`, `RecordLowCostUsage`, `ActivateEntitlementPolicy`, exactly as the APPLICATION_LAYER.md state-changing operation registry declares for `Workflows::Wf015`. The low-cost read coordinator `Workflows::Wf015::LowCostRead` authenticates and authorizes, obtains the immutable Decision, materializes the AuthorizedDTO through the context query handler, then atomically appends the one LowCostUsageRecord, `EntitlementCommitted`, the required query event intent, authorization/audit evidence and Session activity at the durable response checkpoint.
MTX-040.command_input: Enforcement: the resolved snapshot of plan, entitlement, operation class, counter group and window, soft and hard limits, requested units and actor scope, taken at the checkpoint and not earlier. Policy: the candidate, expected current version and plan approval reference. Low-cost read: no client idempotency key is accepted - OD-019 prohibits client-supplied keys on GET and mints the Decision ID server-side from Organization, human Account or service identity, declared operation, resolved target identity and state version, and counter window.
MTX-040.command_output: One immutable Decision (`allow`, `allow_with_warning` or `block`); for high-cost allowance one Reservation in `reserved`; for an allowed low-cost read one LowCostUsageRecord keyed by Decision ID; for policy activation one active version and one superseded prior version. Queueing a high-cost action outputs nothing: it creates no Decision and no reservation.
MTX-040.actor: The tenant-scoped entitlement service identity is the only actor that makes an entitlement Decision; the human Account or service identity named in the envelope is the SUBJECT of the Decision, not its author. A BillingOperator holding `policy.entitlement.manage`, or the authorized billing adapter acting for an already approved plan version, activates policy. An OrganizationAdmin is not an actor here at all: the Permission Baseline denies `policy.entitlement.manage` to every role except BillingOperator, and an OrganizationAdmin may only read allowed notices through `entitlement.notice.read`.
MTX-040.organization_scope: The Organization named in the envelope, which must have its WF-001-created active baseline BillingEntity linked to the current Plan Assignment, per CAP-024 Preconditions. Exactly one Plan Assignment is active per Organization and its BillingEntity MUST be that Organization's one nonclosed BillingEntity; that invariant is MTX-053's, owned by S-02, and is consumed here as a precondition rather than re-enforced. An inactive Organization is not a precondition failure - it is evaluated into a Block Decision with `organization_inactive`.
MTX-040.aggregate: BillingEntity is the canonical write entry for entitlement state, per the APPLICATION_LAYER.md canonical write-entry registry row 'Billing and approved commercial linkage'. EntitlementPolicy is an immutable versioned Policy Artifact. EntitlementDecision, LowCostUsageRecord, LowCostFallbackSnapshot and EntitlementLeaseHeartbeat are immutable appends; EntitlementCounterWindow, EntitlementReservation and EntitlementCommitIntent are mutable children of that root.
MTX-040.aggregate_boundary: The counter window row is the serialization guard, exactly as the `Workflows::Wf015` registry row states ('BillingEntity/counter-window serialization; each decision/usage identity commits once'). A Decision, its reservation delta and the counter window advance commit in one transaction against that guard, so no reservation can exist without the counter row that admitted it. The gated operation's own aggregate is never joined: WF-015 hands back a Decision and a reservation identity, and the Crawl, Evaluation, AIResponse or Export commits its own root under its own workflow carrying the root Decision/reservation ID.
MTX-040.value_objects: EntitlementDecisionId, OperationClass, OperationString, UsageUnit, CounterGroupId, CounterWindow, RequestedUnits, SoftLimit, HardLimit, GraceBehavior, ReasonCode, RecoveryAction, ReservationId, LeaseGeneration, HeartbeatGeneration, PrestartLifetime, MaximumExecutionDuration, DurableCommitPoint, CachedSnapshotId, CachedSnapshotAge, RetryOfDecisionId, PolicyVersion, PlanVersion, PlanApprovalId.
MTX-040.domain_service: Not applicable - WF-015 names no domain service. The short-circuit precedence, the allow predicate, the nullability derivation, the recovery mapping and the cached-snapshot age test are pure total functions over the resolved snapshot, applied inside the `Commercial` context handler under the counter-window lock.
MTX-040.repository: `BillingEntityRepository` is the canonical write path and loads the entitlement child graph; the counter window, reservation and commit-intent rows are checkpoints of that root and expose no independent `save`. Read-only: `EntitlementPolicyRepository`, `PlanAssignmentRepository`, `LowCostFallbackSnapshotRepository`, and the immutable append paths for `entitlement_decisions`, `entitlement_lease_heartbeats` and `low_cost_usage_records`.
MTX-040.persistence_model: Canonical tables per schemas/POSTGRESQL_SCHEMA.md, all `organization_id`-scoped: `entitlement_counter_windows` (`T-MUT`; unique `(organization_id,counter_group,window_start,window_end)`, carrying reserved/committed/low-cost units and `reconciliation_state`), `entitlement_decisions` (`T-IMM`, `LINEAGE`; actor/service XOR, cached snapshot ID/age nullable, retry-of ID nullable), `entitlement_reservations` (`T-MUT`, `LINEAGE`; `state CHECK ('reserved','executing','committed','released','expired')`, one reservation per Decision), `entitlement_lease_heartbeats` (`T-IMM`; unique `(entitlement_reservation_id,heartbeat_generation)`), `low_cost_fallback_snapshots` (`T-IMM`; whole-tuple payload/hash, unique tuple hash), `low_cost_usage_records` (`T-IMM`; unique Decision), `entitlement_commit_intents` (`T-MUT`; unique reservation/output), `plan_assignments` (`T-MUT`; partial unique active per Organization). The Decision, the fallback snapshot and the usage record are append-only by table class: a Decision is never edited to reflect a later reservation outcome, which is why reservation state is read from its own row rather than from the Decision.
MTX-040.migration: Not applicable at this row - schemas/POSTGRESQL_SCHEMA.md already declares all nine entitlement and commercial tables with their constraints, including the `(organization_id,counter_group,window_start,window_end)` uniqueness that makes the counter window addressable and the unique Decision that makes the usage record replay-safe. No product schema object is added by S-22.
MTX-040.transaction_boundary: Enforcement: one `Platform::UnitOfWork` per checkpoint, opened at the checkpoint and never at queue time. It acquires the Organization and counter-window rows in the declared Rails total order, resolves the snapshot under those locks, appends the immutable Decision, and for a high-cost allowance creates the Reservation and advances `active_reserved_units` in the same commit. Commit or release advances `committed_units` and terminates the reservation in one transaction against the same counter window. The low-cost record, `EntitlementCommitted`, the query event intent, authorization/audit evidence and Session activity commit together at the durable response checkpoint that makes the response returnable; if response materialization or that commit fails, no response is returnable and no usage record commits. Policy: one transaction assigning commit-time effectiveness, activating the new version, superseding the prior and emitting `EntitlementPolicyActivated`. No provider or network call sits in any of these transactions - CAP-024's Success Condition and OD-008 both require entitlement to work without a billing-provider call.
MTX-040.concurrency: The counter window row is the serialization point and the reason the hard bound is true rather than approximately true: concurrent high-cost decisions for one `(organization_id, counter_group, window_start, window_end)` serialize against that row, so `committed_units + active_reserved_units + requested_units` is evaluated against a value no other in-flight decision can invalidate, and N concurrent requests at the boundary admit only those that fit. Reservation lifecycle races are decided by fixed winners, not by arrival: at exactly the prestart expiry instant, execution-start loses to expiry; at exactly 15 minutes since the last accepted heartbeat, or at the maximum execution instant, the lease-expiry handler wins over both a new heartbeat and a protected side effect. A heartbeat renews inside a parent-row lock transaction that reads and stores `prior_lease_expires_at`, verifies the exact reservation generation, `executing` state and winning deadline, inserts the immutable heartbeat row and advances the parent to the stored strictly later expiry; the prior expiry is never reconstructed after parent mutation. Nesting cannot double meter: `reassessment.start` subsumes its internally invoked WF-005 through WF-008 core and those stages MUST NOT also reserve or commit `crawl.start`, and every stage records the root Decision/reservation ID.
MTX-040.idempotency: Three distinct identities, none of them interchangeable. (1) Enforcement replay: exact replay with the same idempotency key returns the immutable original Decision plus the CURRENT linked Reservation state and consumes nothing further. (2) Terminal-key exhaustion: after a Block, or once a Reservation reaches `released` or `expired`, a new attempt MUST use a NEW idempotency key and set `retry_of_decision_id` to the preceding Decision; reuse of the terminal key never creates or reopens a reservation. Executing with an expired linked Reservation returns the original Allow Decision plus current Reservation state and domain conflict `reservation_expired`, creating no new Decision and no side effect - only the new-key retry creates a fresh Decision. (3) Low-cost read identity: no client key exists, because OD-019 prohibits client-supplied idempotency keys on GET; the Decision ID is server-minted deterministically from Organization, human Account or service identity, declared operation, resolved target identity and state version, and counter window, and a repeated tuple within the window replays the stored record without another increment or event. Decision ID is the LowCostUsageRecord's uniqueness key, so a transport retry of an identical read cannot be counted twice.
MTX-040.background_job: `entitlement_reconcile` (queue class `control`) claims one `work_executions` row on the reservation/generation identity and invokes exactly one of `HeartbeatEntitlement`, `CommitEntitlement` or `ReleaseEntitlement`, selected solely from persisted Reservation state and deadline - the job chooses no product outcome of its own. It is dispatched by the `entitlement_lease_expire` scheduled action. `entitlement_invariant_sweep_due` runs `invariant_sweep` on the `maintenance` queue every 15 seconds and ensures or invokes the exact reservation expiry/commit/release action identity; it detects a missing action, it does not decide one.
MTX-040.queue: `control` (Sidekiq queue `worker_control`, concurrency 5, 30-second claim) for `entitlement_reconcile`; `maintenance` for `entitlement_invariant_sweep_due`. Queue identity and topology are owned by BACKGROUND_PROCESSING.md; this row renames nothing.
MTX-040.retry_policy: Not applicable as a workflow retry - WF-015 defines no retry of an entitlement Decision, and inventing one would be a second consumption. A denied Decision is terminal for its key; the only forward path is the Recovery Path (upgrade or correct the plan, wait for a new usage window, release an executing reservation when the operation terminates, or restore the authoritative counter) followed by a NEW-key attempt carrying `retry_of_decision_id`. Physical deadlock or serialization retry on the counter-window lock reuses the same command/idempotency claim and never becomes a new product attempt.
MTX-040.terminal_failure: High-cost hard threshold, inactive Organization, inactive actor, unauthorized service, inactive entitlement, unknown operation, missing or invalid policy or counter, stale reservation or counter conflict blocks BEFORE the first protected side effect with its exact reason. A low-cost read whose LowCostFallbackSnapshot has expired returns a Block Decision with `policy_unavailable` or `counter_unavailable` plus outward reason `entitlement_unavailable`. Reservation terminals are `committed`, `released` and `expired`, and all three are terminal. Cancellation or any terminal failure before the listed durable commit point RELEASES exactly once even when intermediate Documents or other partial artifacts exist: those artifacts remain governed by their own workflow but are not a usage commitment.
MTX-040.reconciliation: The lease-expiry handler is the reconciler and its rule is exact: it commits exactly once ONLY if the durable commit point committed strictly before the winning instant, and otherwise releases exactly once. `entitlement_commit_intents` records the durable output type, ID and hash with `state CHECK ('pending','committed','released')` and unique reservation/output, so the commit decision is read from persisted evidence of the output rather than inferred from timing. Low-cost accounting reconciles forward, never backward: while authoritative reconciliation is delayed, counter resolution still includes every LowCostUsageRecord exactly once by record ID, and the cached counter view additionally includes every unreconciled record for the same Organization and window committed strictly after snapshot capture, once by record ID. `entitlement_counter_windows.reconciliation_state` carries that status.
MTX-040.domain_events: Exactly the ten WF-015 events: `EntitlementPolicyActivated`, `EntitlementChecked`, `EntitlementWarningIssued`, `EntitlementViolationDetected`, `EntitlementReserved`, `EntitlementExecutionStarted`, `EntitlementLeaseRenewed`, `EntitlementCommitted`, `EntitlementReleased`, `EntitlementReservationExpired`. `EntitlementCommitted` carries a null reservation ID for a low-cost usage record, which is what distinguishes low-cost accounting from a reservation commit on the same event type. Exact replay emits none. A denied policy command emits no `EntitlementPolicyActivated` and exactly one denial audit event.
MTX-040.event_payload: The canonical logical event envelope with the real `organization_id` (an Organization always exists at an entitlement checkpoint, so the OD-013 bootstrap substitution is unavailable here), plus the Decision ID, the human Account or service identity, operation, usage unit, counter group and window bounds, policy and plan versions, soft and hard limits, before and after counters, requested units, reservation ID where one exists, cached snapshot ID and age where the fallback was used, retry lineage, reason code, recovery action and correlation ID. `EntitlementLeaseRenewed` copies its generation, prior and renewed expiry, worker service identity and content hashes from the immutable heartbeat row and names that row ID as the created affected entity with `to_state=renewed`.
MTX-040.event_producer: `Workflows::Wf015` is the sole producer of all ten. Counter-window lock waits, Sidekiq claim latency and sweep cadence are technical telemetry and MUST NOT be emitted as domain events.
MTX-040.event_consumers: `notification_route_v1` consumes `EntitlementWarningIssued` and `EntitlementViolationDetected` through the outbox and routes them to the human initiating Account when present, otherwise Project MarketingOperator accounts, plus OrganizationAdmin and BillingOperator accounts, requiring `entitlement.notice.read` at severity `warning` on both baseline channels. The gated workflows do not consume an event: they hold the Decision and reservation ID returned at their own checkpoint.
MTX-040.serializer: Only the policy limb serializes: `ATTR-ActivateEntitlementPolicy` on the way in and the standard terminal command result on the way out. Decisions, reservations and usage records have no transport representation of their own; the actor-visible surface is the separately defined notice field set returned by `QRY-018 EntitlementNoticeCollection` under `entitlement.notice.read`, which is owned elsewhere and is not broadened here.
MTX-040.authorization_entry_point: Two entry points that must not be confused. Enforcement: the server-side entitlement service identity at the checkpoint, inside the unit of work, under the counter-window lock. WF-015's Security Notes are absolute - no client-side trust for entitlement decisions - so no request field, header or cached client assertion may supply or influence a Decision. Policy: the `ActivateEntitlementPolicy` handler, before mutation. Entitlement is not authorization and never substitutes for it: a read is authorized by its own named permission through the sole authorization facade and metered separately by its declared operation, and a Block is a capacity outcome, not a denial of authority.
MTX-040.permission_checks: `policy.entitlement.manage` for policy activation - allowed to BillingOperator alone and denied to OrganizationAdmin, MarketingOperator, TechnicalImplementer, SecurityOperator and the read-only Executive Buyer by the Permission Baseline; the billing adapter service identity may synchronize only the already approved plan version and cannot invent a plan or alter system-governed operation classes. `entitlement.notice.read` for reading allowed notices - allowed to OrganizationAdmin, MarketingOperator, TechnicalImplementer and BillingOperator, denied to SecurityOperator, the Executive Buyer and every service identity. The enforcement checkpoints carry no tenant-actor permission at all: they are reachable only by the entitlement service identity, and the operation being gated has already been authorized by its own permission (`crawl.trigger` for `crawl.start`, `export.create` for `export.generate`, and the named read permission for each low-cost read).
MTX-040.tenant_boundary: Every counter window, Decision, reservation and usage record is keyed by `organization_id` and resolved under proved RLS context. The counter window's uniqueness key includes `organization_id`, so one Organization's usage can never be compared with another's limit or consume another's budget. A nonnull cross-Organization reference in the envelope is `F1-AUTH-403 / tenant_mismatch` with no side effect and creates no Decision. The Plan Assignment's BillingEntity MUST be same-Organization by composite foreign key, so a plan cannot be borrowed across tenants. The `plan-approval-interim-baseline-v1` artifact is authority only for the exact interim bytes and no tenant actor can forge or edit it.
MTX-040.error_contract: The distinction that matters is rejection versus Decision, and Volume I draws it precisely. REJECTIONS creating NO Decision: invalid tenant references, both actor forms or neither, malformed units, or a malformed command envelope - `F1-VALIDATION-400`; cross-Organization reference - `F1-AUTH-403 / tenant_mismatch`. EVALUATED INTO an immutable Block Decision rather than rejected: inactive Organization (`organization_inactive`), inactive actor (`actor_inactive`), unauthorized service (`service_unauthorized`), inactive entitlement (`entitlement_inactive`), unknown operation (`operation_unknown`), missing policy (`policy_unavailable`), unavailable counter (`counter_unavailable`), reservation conflict (`reservation_conflict`), high-cost hard threshold (`hard_limit_exceeded`). A capacity or entitlement bound denying work selects `F1-CAPACITY-429`, severity `warning`, retryable false unless the result names a new eligible window, recovery `wait_for_next_window_or_change_approved_entitlement`; the Decision's own `recovery_action` for hard is `wait_for_window` and the next-window instant is the exclusive end of the current UTC-day window. Execution against an expired linked Reservation is `F1-DOMAIN-409 / reservation_expired` with the original Allow Decision and current Reservation state and no side effect. Low-cost fallback expiry surfaces outward reason `entitlement_unavailable`. `upgrade_plan` without a distinct valid owner-approved Plan Approval artifact deterministically returns `upgrade_plan_unavailable`. Policy denial (stale, future-effective, expiring, incomplete, commercially unapproved, broadened beyond global safety, or unauthorized) changes nothing and emits one denial audit event.
MTX-040.audit_record: Per WF-015 Audit and Observability, persisted in full: every Entitlement Decision field, counter before and after values, recovery action, cached-snapshot ID and age, each LowCostUsageRecord and its reconciliation state, idempotency and retry lineage, every reservation heartbeat and state, the commit or release event, actor and correlation ID. CAP-024's Failure Condition includes an unexplained legitimate block, so a Block that cannot be reconstructed from its own persisted fields is itself the defect: the reason code, the counters that produced it and the snapshot identity are all stored on the immutable Decision rather than recomputed.
MTX-040.observability: Entitlement enforcement metrics and failure telemetry per CAP-024 Observability Requirements. Saturation is observable before denial through `EntitlementWarningIssued` at the soft threshold; denial through `EntitlementViolationDetected`; the reservation lifecycle through `EntitlementReserved`, `EntitlementExecutionStarted`, `EntitlementLeaseRenewed`, `EntitlementCommitted`, `EntitlementReleased` and `EntitlementReservationExpired`. A cached-fallback Decision is distinguishable in telemetry by its `cached_snapshot_id` and `cached_snapshot_age`, so degraded low-cost operation is visible rather than silent. Entitlement counters and reservations MUST NOT be cached in Redis; SECURITY_PERFORMANCE.md forbids it by name and a cache outage cannot consume entitlement or change a decision winner.
MTX-040.retention: Usage counters and entitlement states are retained per CAP-024 Data Implications. The LowCostFallbackSnapshot has a bounded usable age of 24 hours from `snapshot_captured_at`, which is an eligibility bound rather than a retention window. The retention window is owned by 015 DATA_LIFECYCLE.md; this row states none.
MTX-040.test_contracts: TYP-DATA: the OD-006 high-cost predicate at the boundary - `committed + active_reserved + requested == hard_limit` is ALLOWED and `> hard_limit` is blocked, proving equality is admitted rather than rejected. TYP-DATA: `>= soft_limit` returns allow_with_warning, proving soft is inclusive. TYP-DATA: the OD-006 low-cost rule - a read AT and ABOVE the 1,000 hard limit is still allowed with an over-limit warning and still creates exactly one usage record while the Organization is active and the human Account or tenant service identity remains authorized, proving warning-only is implemented as ratified rather than withheld as interim. TYP-DATA: each `entitlement-interim-v1` value - `crawl.start` 3/4, `reassessment.start` 1/2, `ai.generate` 20/25, `export.generate` 8/10, and the five low-cost operations sharing `baseline_reads` at 800/1,000 - asserted at the boundary and one either side. TYP-DATA: the five low-cost operations share ONE counter, proving a `score.read` consumes the same budget as an `issue.read`; each high-cost operation uses its own named counter group, proving they do not. TYP-DATA: the counter window is the half-open UTC day `[00:00:00Z, next 00:00:00Z)` containing the SERVER decision time - a decision at `23:59:59.999Z` and one at `00:00:00.000Z` fall in different windows, and the next-window recovery instant is the exclusive end. TYP-DATA: queueing a high-cost action creates NO Decision and NO reservation, proving the gate is at the protected execution checkpoint and not at enqueue. TYP-DATA: a queued high-cost action re-resolves CURRENT policy at execution and has no earlier authoritative Decision to reuse. TYP-SEC: the short-circuit precedence is exact and total - `organization_inactive` beats `actor_inactive`/`service_unauthorized` beats `entitlement_inactive` beats `operation_unknown` beats `policy_unavailable` beats `counter_unavailable` beats `reservation_conflict` beats `hard_limit_exceeded` beats `soft_limit_reached` beats `within_limit`; a fixture failing two predicates returns only the higher one. TYP-DATA: the recovery mapping is fixed - within/soft->`none`, hard->`wait_for_window`, Organization->`reactivate_organization`, actor->`reactivate_actor`, service or unknown operation->`contact_support`, inactive entitlement->`upgrade_plan`, policy/cached-policy->`restore_policy`, counter/cached-counter->`restore_counter`, reservation conflict->`submit_new_attempt`. TYP-DATA: an inactive Organization, inactive actor, unauthorized service, unknown operation, inactive entitlement, missing policy or unavailable counter each produce an immutable BLOCK DECISION, not a workflow-precondition rejection - the Decision exists and is auditable. TYP-VALIDATION contrast, asserted as TYP-DATA: an invalid tenant reference, both actor forms, neither actor form, malformed units or a malformed envelope create NO Decision at all. TYP-SEC: no client-side trust - a request header, body field or cached client assertion claiming an allowance changes no Decision. TYP-SEC: `policy.entitlement.manage` is BillingOperator-only; an OrganizationAdmin holding every other tenant permission cannot activate, amend or supersede an Entitlement Policy, and holds only `entitlement.notice.read`. MTX-090.aggregate: BillingEntity as the canonical write entry, with the counter window and reservation as the constrained children.
MTX-090.aggregate_boundary: The rule's atomicity clause is what fixes the boundary: the check and the reserve are ONE operation against the counter window, so no interleaving can observe a checked-but-unreserved state. The gated operation's own aggregate stays outside.

The rule is nevertheless enforced BY persistence: `entitlement_reservations` allows one reservation per Decision and `entitlement_counter_windows` is unique per `(organization_id,counter_group,window_start,window_end)`, so the atomic reserve has exactly one row to serialize against.
MTX-090.migration: Not applicable - no schema object is added; the constraints the rule relies on are already declared in schemas/POSTGRESQL_SCHEMA.md.
MTX-090.transaction_boundary: The rule states its own boundary: the check executes server-side with CURRENT policy and counter state and performs an atomic idempotent reserve at the protected execution checkpoint BEFORE side effects. Queue creation opens no transaction and creates neither Decision nor reservation. Commit and release each occur exactly once, in their own transaction against the same counter window.
MTX-090.concurrency: Atomicity is the rule's mechanism and the counter window row is where it lives: check-then-reserve is one serialized operation, so two concurrent requests at the boundary cannot both observe headroom and both reserve. This is what makes 'never reserve or commit above hard limits' true under concurrency rather than true on average. Reservation lifecycle races are decided by the fixed winners at MTX-040 - expiry beats execution-start at the prestart instant, and the lease-expiry handler beats a heartbeat and a side effect at the heartbeat-plus-15-minute and maximum-execution instants.
MTX-090.idempotency: The rule names three separate obligations and this row keeps them separate. The RESERVE is idempotent: the same key at the same checkpoint reserves once and replay returns the original Decision plus current reservation state. TERMINAL-KEY REPLAY never reopens a reservation: once the Decision is a Block or the reservation is `released` or `expired`, that key is spent and returns the stored outcome, never a fresh reservation. A NEW ATTEMPT uses a linked new key with `retry_of_decision_id` pointing at the preceding Decision, so the retry is auditable as a successor rather than indistinguishable from a first attempt. COMMIT/RELEASE occurs exactly once, guarded by the reservation's own terminal state rather than by delivery deduplication, so a redelivered `entitlement_reconcile` job cannot commit twice.
MTX-090.background_job: Not applicable as a job of its own - the rule constrains commands. The commit/release exactly-once obligation is discharged at the checkpoint or by the `entitlement_reconcile` lease handler at MTX-040, whichever wins under the fixed deadline rule.
MTX-090.queue: Not applicable - PRULE-039 introduces no queue. Its queue-time clause is a prohibition, not a queue: queue creation MUST create neither Decision nor reservation.
MTX-090.retry_policy: Not applicable - PRULE-039 defines no retry and expressly forbids the shape of one that would consume twice. A new attempt is a new linked key, which the rule distinguishes from a retry precisely so that replay and retry cannot both consume usage.
MTX-090.terminal_failure: A high-cost operation whose check fails blocks BEFORE the first protected side effect with its exact reason; no provider call, no workflow side effect and no partial artifact precedes the Block. A reservation that reaches `released` or `expired` is terminal and its key is spent.
MTX-090.reconciliation: The commit-or-release decision reconciles against persisted output evidence rather than timing: the lease handler commits exactly once only if the durable commit point committed strictly before the winning instant and otherwise releases exactly once, with `entitlement_commit_intents` recording the durable output type, ID and hash under `state CHECK ('pending','committed','released')` and unique reservation/output.
MTX-090.domain_events: Not applicable - PRULE-039 emits no event of its own; it gates `EntitlementChecked`, `EntitlementReserved`, `EntitlementExecutionStarted`, `EntitlementCommitted`, `EntitlementReleased` and `EntitlementReservationExpired`.
MTX-090.event_payload: Not applicable - no event of its own.
MTX-090.event_producer: Not applicable - no event of its own.
MTX-090.event_consumers: Not applicable - no event of its own.
MTX-090.serializer: Not applicable - no transport exposure; PRULE-039's subject has no client-facing representation by design.
MTX-090.authorization_entry_point: The checkpoint itself, server-side, before the first protected side effect. PRULE-039's SEC-REQ-005 linkage is why the placement is a security property and not a performance one: a check placed after a side effect, or performed anywhere but the server, is a bypass regardless of its arithmetic.
MTX-090.permission_checks: Not applicable - PRULE-039 adds no permission and grants none. The gated operation carries its own permission (`crawl.trigger` for `crawl.start`, `export.create` for `export.generate`, the named read permission for each low-cost read); entitlement is a capacity gate applied after authorization and never in place of it.
MTX-090.tenant_boundary: The counter window is unique per `(organization_id,counter_group,window_start,window_end)`, so the atomic reserve is per Organization by construction and one tenant's concurrent load cannot exhaust another's headroom.

A stale or missing high-cost policy or counter fails CLOSED - PRULE-039 admits no fallback for high-cost, and the low-cost snapshot path is PRULE-040's.

MTX-090.test_contracts: TYP-SEC: the check executes SERVER-SIDE - a client-asserted allowance, header or body field changes no Decision and grants no side effect. TYP-DATA: the check uses CURRENT policy and counter state at the checkpoint - a policy activated between enqueue and execution governs the execution, proving the queued action re-resolves rather than replaying a pinned snapshot. TYP-DATA: queue creation creates NEITHER a Decision NOR a reservation, asserted by counting rows in both tables after enqueue. TYP-DATA: the reserve is atomic and at the protected execution checkpoint BEFORE the first side effect - a fixture that fails the check performs no provider call and leaves no partial artifact. TYP-DATA: the reserve is idempotent - the same key at the same checkpoint reserves exactly once. TYP-DATA: N concurrent pre-execution reserves against one counter window admit only those that fit and never exceed the hard limit; the boundary case where the last admitted request lands exactly ON the hard limit is admitted. TYP-DATA: terminal-key replay never reopens - after a Block, and after `released`, and after `expired`, the same key returns the stored outcome and creates no reservation in all three cases. TYP-DATA: a new attempt uses a NEW key and sets `retry_of_decision_id` to the preceding Decision; a new attempt with a reused terminal key is refused. TYP-DATA: replay and retry cannot both consume - a replay followed by a linked retry consumes exactly one unit, not two. TYP-DATA: commit occurs exactly once - a redelivered `entitlement_reconcile` job against a `committed` reservation commits nothing further. TYP-DATA: release occurs exactly once - the same for a `released` reservation. TYP-DATA: the commit-or-release fork is decided by the STRICTLY-BEFORE test against the durable commit point, not by which handler ran first; a durable output committed exactly AT the winning instant releases. TYP-DATA: nested execution does not double reserve - a `reassessment.start` run never takes a `crawl.start` reservation for its internal WF-005 stage. TYP-SEC: an outage of the policy or counter store fails a high-cost operation CLOSED, with no fallback snapshot admitted and no side effect performed. TYP-OBS: every reserve has exactly one terminal event, and a reserve without one is detected by the 15-second invariant sweep rather than left stranded. TYP-SEC: PRULE-039 grants no authority - holding no operation permission but satisfying the entitlement check still denies the operation.

MTX-091.value_objects: EntitlementDecisionId, ReasonCode, RecoveryAction, UsageUnit, CounterWindow, SoftLimit, HardLimit, RequestedUnits, CachedSnapshotId, CachedSnapshotAge, RetryOfDecisionId, PolicyVersion, PlanVersion.
MTX-091.domain_service: Not applicable - PRULE-040 names no domain service. The nullability derivation and the recovery mapping are pure total functions of the reason code.
MTX-091.repository: The immutable append paths for `entitlement_decisions`, `low_cost_usage_records` and `low_cost_fallback_snapshots`, under the `BillingEntityRepository` root; `EntitlementCounterWindow` read for the before values and advanced for the after values.
MTX-091.persistence_model: `entitlement_decisions` is `T-IMM` with `LINEAGE`, actor/service XOR, cached snapshot ID and age nullable, retry-of ID nullable. `low_cost_usage_records` is `T-IMM` with a UNIQUE Decision, which is the physical expression of the rule's replay-safety requirement rather than an incidental index. `low_cost_fallback_snapshots` is `T-IMM` with a unique whole-tuple hash, which is the physical expression of 'never combines values captured at different instants'.
MTX-091.migration: Not applicable - schemas/POSTGRESQL_SCHEMA.md already declares the unique Decision on `low_cost_usage_records` and the unique tuple hash on `low_cost_fallback_snapshots`. No schema object is added.
MTX-091.transaction_boundary: The Decision commits with the counter-window read that produced its before values, so its before/after pair is never a reconstruction. The LowCostUsageRecord commits at the SAME durable checkpoint that makes the authorized response returnable, together with `EntitlementCommitted`, the query event intent, authorization/audit evidence and Session activity - a response that is returnable without its record, or a record without a returnable response, is a violation of this rule in either direction.
MTX-091.concurrency: A low-cost Decision does not serialize a reservation because it takes none: its immutable decision-time before and after counters are EQUAL, and all usage accounting happens later, at the durable response checkpoint, through the separate record. Concurrent identical reads resolve to the same server-minted Decision ID under OD-019, so the unique Decision on `low_cost_usage_records` admits exactly one of them and the loser replays the stored record.
MTX-091.idempotency: Decision ID is the LowCostUsageRecord's uniqueness key, and under OD-019 that ID is minted deterministically from Organization, human Account or service identity, declared operation, resolved target identity and state version, and counter window. That composition is what makes the record replay-safe with no client key: a repeated tuple within the window replays the stored record with no second increment and no second event, while a different target or a different state version is a genuinely different read and gets its own record. Exact command replay returns the stored response and record.
MTX-091.background_job: Not applicable - PRULE-040 constrains record content and defines no asynchronous work. The delayed authoritative reconciliation it tolerates is a property of counter resolution, not a job of this rule's.
MTX-091.queue: Not applicable - no queue of its own.
MTX-091.retry_policy: Not applicable - the rule defines no retry. A transport retry of a low-cost read is not a new usage: it resolves to the same server-minted Decision ID and replays the stored record.
MTX-091.terminal_failure: A denied read creates NO record. A request that never reaches the durable authorized-response checkpoint creates no record, including a conditional response that returns no representation. If response materialization or the durable commit fails, no response is returnable and no record commits. A Block commits its Decision but no usage record and returns no DTO.
MTX-091.reconciliation: Counter resolution includes each LowCostUsageRecord exactly once BY RECORD ID, including while authoritative reconciliation is delayed - the delay changes the reconciliation state, never the count. The cached counter view additionally includes every unreconciled record for the same Organization and window committed strictly after snapshot capture, once by record ID, which is what stops a fallback Decision from under-counting reads that landed after the snapshot was taken.
MTX-091.domain_events: Not applicable as an event of its own - PRULE-040 constrains the fields carried by the MTX-040 events and requires `EntitlementCommitted` with a NULL reservation ID for each allowed low-cost read.
MTX-091.event_payload: Not applicable - no event of its own; the payload obligations are at MTX-040.
MTX-091.event_producer: Not applicable - no event of its own.
MTX-091.event_consumers: Not applicable - no event of its own.
MTX-091.serializer: Not applicable - no transport exposure. The actor-visible subset of these fields is the separately defined notice field set behind `entitlement.notice.read`, which this rule does not broaden.
MTX-091.authorization_entry_point: Not applicable - PRULE-040 is a record-content rule and performs no authorization. The read it accounts for is authorized separately by its own named permission through the sole authorization facade, before the coordinator obtains the Decision.
MTX-091.permission_checks: Not applicable - PRULE-040 adds no permission. The five low-cost operation strings are metering classes, not permissions: `report.view`, `history.view` and `score.read` do not exist in the Permission Baseline at all, and the coincidence of `issue.read` and `recommendation.read` with real permission tokens grants nothing.
MTX-091.tenant_boundary: Every Decision, snapshot and usage record carries its Organization, and the cached counter view is scoped to the same Organization and window as the snapshot, so a fallback can never pull another tenant's unreconciled records into a count.
MTX-091.error_contract: The rule's own subject: reason code is EXACTLY one of `within_limit`, `soft_limit_reached`, `hard_limit_exceeded`, `organization_inactive`, `actor_inactive`, `service_unauthorized`, `entitlement_inactive`, `policy_unavailable`, `counter_unavailable`, `cached_policy_snapshot_used`, `cached_counter_snapshot_used`, `operation_unknown`, `reservation_conflict`; recovery action is exactly one of `none`, `wait_for_window`, `upgrade_plan`, `reactivate_organization`, `reactivate_actor`, `restore_policy`, `restore_counter`, `submit_new_attempt`, `contact_support`, and the mapping between them is fixed rather than chosen. An expired low-cost fallback returns a Block with `policy_unavailable` or `counter_unavailable` plus outward reason `entitlement_unavailable`.
MTX-091.audit_record: The Decision IS the audit record for the check, which is why immutability and completeness are the same requirement here: every field, the counters before and after, the recovery action, the cached-snapshot ID and age, the idempotency key and the retry lineage are persisted on the row and are never recomputed. Each LowCostUsageRecord and its reconciliation state are persisted alongside.
MTX-091.observability: OBS-REQ-004 is discharged by field completeness rather than by a metric: a cached-fallback Decision is identifiable by its nonnull `cached_snapshot_id` and `cached_snapshot_age`, a retry by its nonnull `retry_of_decision_id`, and a low-cost commit by `EntitlementCommitted` with a null reservation ID. Degraded operation is therefore visible in the record itself.
MTX-091.retention: Not applicable - PRULE-040 defines no retention obligation. The 24-hour fallback bound is an eligibility test on `cached_snapshot_age`, not a retention window; window ownership is 015 DATA_LIFECYCLE.md's.
MTX-091.test_contracts: TYP-DATA: a Decision is immutable and is exactly one of `allow`, `allow_with_warning`, `block` - no fourth value and no later mutation, including after its reservation commits or expires. TYP-DATA: the always-nonnull set holds for EVERY reason code - Organization/actor identity, operation, requested units, idempotency and retry lineage, decision, reason, recovery and timestamps. TYP-DATA: actor/service XOR - exactly one of human Account ID or service-identity ID is present on every Decision. TYP-DATA: the reason-specific null rules, each asserted separately. Organization/actor/service failure: ALL plan, policy, rule, counter, reservation and cache fields null. Inactive entitlement: assigned plan version retained when present; policy, rule, counter, reservation and cache null. Unknown operation: plan version retained; usage unit, policy, rule, counter, reservation and cache null. Unavailable policy: plan version retained; policy version, rule, counter, reservation and cache null UNLESS the bounded cached fallback is used, in which case the complete cached versions and values, snapshot ID and age are stored. Unavailable counter: plan, policy and rule fields stored; all FOUR before/after counter fields and the reservation and cache fields null unless the same complete cached fallback is used. TYP-DATA: every OTHER Block has nonnull before counters with AFTER counters EQUAL to before, and null reservation and cache fields - proving a Block never moves a counter. TYP-DATA: a high-cost Allow or AllowWithWarning has after active-reserved units equal to before PLUS requested units, a nonnull reservation, and UNCHANGED committed units - proving reserve is not commit. TYP-DATA: a low-cost Decision has NO reservation and equal decision-time before and after counters - proving the Decision does not account and the record does. TYP-DATA: the thirteen reason codes are exhaustive and the nine recovery actions are exhaustive; no fixture produces a value outside either set. TYP-DATA: the fixed recovery mapping for all thirteen reasons. TYP-DATA: exactly one LowCostUsageRecord per allowed low-cost response, containing Decision ID, Organization, operation, usage unit, counter window, requested units, idempotency key and commit time. TYP-DATA: Decision ID is the record's uniqueness key - a second insert for the same Decision ID is refused by the unique constraint, not by application logic. TYP-DATA: an allowed low-cost read emits `EntitlementCommitted` with a NULL reservation ID. TYP-DATA: exact replay returns the stored response and record with NO second increment and NO second event. TYP-DATA: a DENIED read creates no record. TYP-DATA: a request that never reaches the durable authorized-response checkpoint creates no record, including a conditional response returning no representation. TYP-DATA: a Block commits its Decision, no record and no DTO. TYP-DATA: failure of response materialization or of the durable commit leaves no returnable response and no record. TYP-OBS: the record commits at the SAME checkpoint as the response - neither can exist without the other, asserted in both directions. TYP-DATA: whole-tuple cache identity - the snapshot is captured only when policy and authoritative counter are simultaneously valid; a Decision never mixes a current component with a cached one; the one snapshot ID and age govern every cached field. TYP-DATA: `cached_snapshot_age = decision_time - snapshot_captured_at`, exactly 24 hours allowed, greater expired. TYP-DATA: both dependencies unavailable resolves to `cached_policy_snapshot_used`, proving policy wins. TYP-DATA: the cached counter view includes each unreconciled record for the same Organization and window committed strictly after capture, once by record ID - a read landing after capture is counted, and counted once. TYP-DATA: counter resolution includes each record exactly once even while authoritative reconciliation is delayed. TYP-DATA: a stale counter path never silently omits a record. TYP-INT: the missing-counter fixture - `counter_unavailable` for a high-cost operation Blocks with all four counter fields null and no reservation. TYP-OBS: every warning and every denial is reconstructible from its own persisted Decision fields alone, with no recomputation against live policy. TYP-SEC: the actor-visible surface exposes only the separately defined notice fields under `entitlement.notice.read`; a Decision's internal fields are asserted absent from that projection.
MTX-091.rollout: As MTX-040. The low-cost accounting limb is fully contracted here under OD-019; its GET transport activates with the API_CONTRACTS.md Volume II baseline. MTX-097 (PRULE-046) carries the generic envelope obligation across all slices and is not duplicated by this row.
